summary.text: Jason Lewis is a Democratic member of the Massachusetts Senate for the Fifth Middlesex District, which includes Malden, Melrose, Reading, Stoneham, Wakefield and parts of Winchester, and was first elected to the Senate in 2014.
The Legislature's committee listing shows him as Chair of the Senate Committee on Ethics and of the Joint Committee on Education.

paragraphs.text: Jason Lewis's official biography says he was born in South Africa and came to the United States with his family at age twelve.
It says he attended public schools and graduated magna cum laude from Harvard College, and it lists a B.A. from Harvard in 1990 and an M.B.A. from Harvard in 1995.

The biography says that before public service he began in management consulting and held senior management roles at RSA Security and then at Endeca Technologies, where he was Senior Vice President of Marketing.
It says he served five years in the Massachusetts House of Representatives before his election to the Senate.
The biography says he led the 2019 Student Opportunity Act and the 2018 effort to raise the state minimum wage to $15 an hour and create a paid family and medical leave program.
It says he is a member of Senate President Karen Spilka's leadership team and co-founded the legislature's Zero Waste Caucus and Middlesex Fells Caucus.
He lives in Winchester with his wife Susan, and the biography lists two daughters.
